scenarios.name: Fictional DIVARTY fires coordination CPX
scenarios.objective: Study information exchange among a fictional fires headquarters, subordinate organizations, and supporting systems.
questions: Which organizations own each system and service?
What documented interfaces and versions need verification?
How would an application fault differ from a transport fault?
What evidence would support acceptance testing?

scenarios.name: Fictional brigade communications exercise
scenarios.objective: Study generic communications dependencies across a fictional brigade headquarters and subordinate units.
questions: Which essential information exchanges are simulated?
Which service dependencies are single points of failure?

scenarios.name: Fictional intelligence staff CPX
scenarios.objective: Explore mission application availability and authorized information sharing in a synthetic environment.
questions: What are the identity and storage dependencies?
How is a service problem distinguished from a network problem?

faults.name: Synthetic name resolution failure
faults.symptom: Training application can be reached by simulated IP but not hostname.
checks: Compare name lookup to IP reachability
faults.lesson: Network reachability alone does not guarantee application usability.

faults.name: Synthetic authentication outage
faults.symptom: Users can reach the training application but cannot sign in.
faults.lesson: Application access depends on identity services as well as transport.

faults.name: Synthetic edge power failure
faults.symptom: A fictional node and its connected users lose all service.
checks: Verify service restoration after power recovery
faults.lesson: Start troubleshooting at the lowest failed dependency.
